transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Jordan Patel (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE); Priya Raman (Redwood Integration Eng); Anita Lopez (Rivergate Head Infra); Ravi Kumar (Rivergate SRE); Sofia Marin (Rivergate PM); Tim Rhodes (Rivergate Security); Ellen Park (Rivergate Network)

Summary:
Quick run-through of onboarding plan for Rivergate's pilot using Redwood (hosted + dedicated options discussed). Focus areas: VPC peering, KMS/encryption requirements, audit logs, SSO mapping, and model sizing for throughput targets. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics covered:
- Onboarding runbook and network intake
- Private vs Dedicated tradeoffs and timelines
- Security/compliance checklist (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Initial smoke test and perf targets
- Next steps and artifacts to share

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining we have about 55 minutes, i'll run through the ignition plan then hand to liam for model sizing and priya for network details.
[00:12] Anita Lopez: cool thanks maya, we are excited to get this in the pilot lane, quick heads up our timeline is end of Q2 for a limited roll out.
[00:22] Jordan Patel: great, so it's an aggressive timeline but doable, we'll prioritize the smoke tests and the onboarding runbook.
[00:30] Ravi Kumar: just fyi we've got pretty strict egress rules, need to confirm whether hosted API calls can go through our proxy or if we need VPC peering.
[00:42] Maya Chen: yeah that's one of the main things we wanted to cover. for Rivergate most customers pick one of three modes: hosted API for fastest time to value, dedicated reserved pools for throughput predictability, or private (VPC) for full isolation.
[00:58] Tim Rhodes: when you say private can you clarify, like do you manage the control plane or do we run an on-prem agent? security team needs to know where keys live.
[01:12] Priya Raman: quick answer — in Private mode the control plane can be customer-managed and we support KMS integrations or bring-your-own-HSM. some customers also prefer our VPC peering option with customer-managed subnets.
[01:28] Sofia Marin: our success criteria are clear: latency under 300ms p95 for the routing layer and less than 2x the cost of our baseline inference. those are the two knobs we care about.
[01:40] Liam O'Neill: understood. for model sizing, can you confirm average context length and concurrency for pilot? that drives batch configs and whether you need a dedicated pool.
[01:52] Anita Lopez: pilot will be 50 concurrent users, typical prompts 512 tokens, spikes to 120 concurrent for brief windows.
[02:03] Liam O'Neill: okay that helps. rough rule of thumb, for ~50-100 concurrency at 512, a dedicated small GPU pool may be cheaper at scale because of batching and KV cache reuse; hosted is fine for early low-throughput evals.
[02:18] Ravi Kumar: cost aside, we have data residency and audit constraints — we need logs forwarded to our SIEM and reversible deletion controls for tokens older than 180 days.
[02:30] Maya Chen: we can do audit log forwarding, and we have retention controls in the console. note — some names in the console show up as Redwood Analytics, sometimes transcripts label it differently but the exports include per-token metadata.
[02:45] Tim Rhodes: we need SOC 2 type II evidence and an ISO statement, is that publicly available? and we need an initial security questionnaire answered.
[02:58] Jordan Patel: yes we will attach our SOC2 report and an abbreviated security packet. i'll follow up with a completed security questionnaire for your vendor team.
[03:09] Anita Lopez: good. on networking, Ellen and Ravi will need the peering ip ranges and the egress endpoints if we go hosted.
[03:20] Priya Raman: i'll paste that in the network intake sheet. quick note — for hosted endpoints there are a small set of egress ranges and optional proxy patterns. for VPC peering we'll give you subnet/CIDR guidance.
[03:35] Ellen Park: ok pls include the BGP / routing hints, and whether private dns is required.
[03:42] Priya Raman: yes we'll include that. also, if you intend to use our prefix/KV cache feature, we recommend a short warm-up run to benefit from reuse.
[03:56] Liam O'Neill: (to santa) caching note — the KV cache is most effective if requests share prefixes; if you have many varied prompts we won't see the same win. but for product flows that are templated it's great.
[04:10] Sofia Marin: our flows are fairly templated so caching could help. can you estimate the throughput win?
[04:16] Liam O'Neill: ballpark, if prefix reuse is ~40% you could see 20-30% token cost reduction in some cases — not guaranteed but we can benchmark.
[04:30] Maya Chen: ok switching to rollout plan — step 1: onboarding intake and runbook completion, step 2: test/staging smoke test, step 3: pilot in dedicated pool if chosen, then production roll.
[04:45] Anita Lopez: timeline question, how long to spin up a dedicated pool?
[04:50] Liam O'Neill: provisioning is typically 3-5 business days for reserved capacity after order and network validation, faster if it's standard configs.
[04:59] Ravi Kumar: and what about certs and KMS? we want keys in our KMS.
[05:05] Priya Raman: we support customer-managed KMS for keys at rest; for request-level encryption we can integrate with your HSM via standard APIs, will require an ops runbook.
[05:18] Tim Rhodes: i'd like to schedule a security-only session with your security engineer. can we do that next week?
[05:25] Jordan Patel: yes we can set that up. maya i'll put that on the calendar.
[05:30] Maya Chen: perfect. next i'll hand to liam to talk model footprint and perf numbers, then priya will cover the network intake specifics.

[05:42] Liam O'Neill: okay model footprint — you're evaluating two model families right? one open source variant and one quantized variant that you want to try?
[05:52] Sofia Marin: yes, our ML team prefers the quantized 8-bit variant for cost reasons, but we may validate an FP16 variant for quality-check.
[06:02] Liam O'Neill: that makes sense. for 8-bit quant you can get sizable memory savings but expect some delta in generation quality — we can A/B test in pilot. throughput for quantized model is typically 1.3-1.8x tokens/sec improvement depending on kernel selection.
[06:20] Ravi Kumar: how deterministic are the kernels across GPU types? we have mix of A100 and some older 80GB instances in our infra for internal benching.
[06:32] Liam O'Neill: kernel behavior varies; our runtime picks kernels by model and hardware. we'll record the exact kernel and perf profile in the onboarding doc. if you want deterministic results use pinned hardware in Dedicated.
[06:48] Anita Lopez: what's the rollback plan if we see latency regressions in prod?
[06:54] Maya Chen: we have automatic fallback policies — if a new model variant exceeds latency SLA it falls back to a compatible variant or a smaller model. we can configure canary percentages.
[07:07] Sofia Marin: awesome. can we get a sample canary policy?
[07:10] Jordan Patel: yes i'll include a sample canary and an A/B plan in the runbook.
[07:16] Priya Raman: network intake — i'll share a templated spreadsheet. required fields: allowed egress IPs, peering subnets, NTP/ntp rules, proxy hostnames, and whether you want mTLS.
[07:30] Ellen Park: we will require mTLS for peering endpoints. please document the cert exchange process.
[07:36] Priya Raman: will do, and we'll note whether certs are short lived.
[07:41] Ravi Kumar: about token retention — we need to ensure that any PII is scrubbed and that logs forwarded to our SIEM are redacted for sensitive fields.
[07:52] Maya Chen: we have PII redaction settings and token retention controls; however transcripts sometimes include raw input depending on config, so we'll show how to turn that off and only forward metadata.
[08:07] Tim Rhodes: you mentioned audit logs earlier — we need them to be pushed to our S3 with object-lock for 90 days.
[08:15] Jordan Patel: we can forward logs to your S3 or your SIEM; object-lock might need additional vendor paperwork but we can coordinate with our ops team.
[08:26] Anita Lopez: okay let's talk success metrics for pilot: SLA p95 latency <300ms, error rate <0.5%, and cost per 1k tokens under your proposed baseline.
[08:40] Liam O'Neill: we'll put together a cost estimate for both hosted and dedicated for your token volumes — i'll include estimated cost per 1k as well as expected latency ranges.
[08:49] Sofia Marin: great. also can we run a short perf test with our dev team next week? 1 hour window.
[08:55] Maya Chen: yes we recommend a 1-hour smoke test window to warm caches. which day works?
[09:00] Ravi Kumar: tuesday morning for us is good.
[09:04] Jordan Patel: i'll propose tuesday 09:00-10:00 PDT in a follow-up invite.
[09:10] Priya Raman: one more network note — if you do peering we need a maintenance window to swap routes; that usually is 30 minutes of possible disruption.
[09:20] Ellen Park: that's fine, we'll schedule it overnight.
[09:24] Maya Chen: nearing the end here — quick recap of owners and due dates, then open floor for final q's.
[09:31] Jordan Patel: recap items: runbook & network sheet from redwood by 3/30, console invite 3/29, SRE deep-dive/smoke test scheduling, and security questionnaire + SOC2 docs.
[09:43] Anita Lopez: will your runbook include example terraform or IaC snippets for peering?
[09:48] Priya Raman: yes we'll add examples and a minimal terraform snippet for peering + route tables.
[09:55] Tim Rhodes: final q — who is the escalation contact if something breaks during pilot?
[10:00] Maya Chen: primary escalation is jordan for onboarding and liam for technical, and there's a 24/7 on-call for Dedicated which we'll share as part of the SLA docs.
[10:12] Sofia Marin: thanks all, this was useful.
[10:15] Maya Chen: thanks everyone — next steps in calendar, i'll follow up with artifacts.

End of transcript.
